newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan caretakers frame information freedom law.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan caretakers frame information freedom law.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker cabinet approved legislation on Wednesday to allow better access for citizens to government papers.
A government statement, quoted by the official APP news agency, said the legislation would be issued as a presidential ordinance, which must be approved by the two houses of parliament to become law.

The lower house of parliament was dismissed by President Farooq Leghari on November 5, when he sacked prime minister Benazir Bhutto's government on disputed charges of corruption and misrule. A new house is to be elected on February 3.
Wednesday's cabinet meeting approved the draft of the Freedom of Information Ordinance "providing the citizens improved access to public records", the statement said.
It said the government "believes that such access to public records promotes transparency in government affairs and enhances accountability of the holders of public offices".
The statement said the draft of the law had been prepared in consultation with newspaper editors and proprietors who have been demanding such legislation to promote freedom of information.

The law provides that any Pakistani citizen "may request any public office for information contained in any public record, including copy of any such record" and "the public office shall provide necessary information and copy of the public record", the statement said.

But it said such access would not be allowed to documents which are classified, relate to an individual's privacy or have been given to a public office by a person on condition that they will not be disclosed to a third party.
If a public office fails to give the information sought, a citizen could approach to an ombudsman whose decision would be final, the statement said.
